Terraform Grafana Dashboard Deployment Architecture
Dashboard JSON → root dashboards.tf → shared module → grafana_dashboard → Grafana provider → Grafana Cloud | Remote state is a separate path

Other dashboard definitions
*.json files in the repo

Responsibilities
• Reads dashboard JSON with file(...)
• Creates the dashboards map (one entry per file)
• Groups dashboards by team
• Assigns folder_uid for the team folder
• Passes the Grafana provider alias
• Calls the reusable module

module "sre" {
source = "./shared/dashboard-set"
dashboards = { fisgw = file("FISGW.json") }
folder_uid = "<sre folder uid>"
providers = { grafana = grafana.pavilionpaynp }
}
Shared module: shared/dashboard-set - creates one grafana_dashboard per map entry

variables.tf
variable "dashboards" (map of dashboard JSON)
variable "folder_uid" (target Grafana folder)

main.tf
resource "grafana_dashboard" "dashboard" {
for_each = var.dashboards
folder = var.folder_uid · config_json = each.value
}

Bridge
Translates each resource into an authenticated
Grafana HTTP API call.

Provider responsibilities
• Authentication
• API communication
• Resource management

Grafana responsibilities
• Validate dashboard JSON
• Store dashboard
• Organize by folder
• Display dashboards to users
Dashboards land in the folder chosen by folder_uid:

SRE folder
dashboards for the SRE team
(folder_uid decides)

Tap2Play folder
dashboards for Tap2Play
(folder_uid decides)

VIP Connect folder
dashboards for VIP Connect
(folder_uid decides)

backend.tf
backend "azurerm": storage account,
container and state key

Important
Azure Storage holds Terraform state only.
It does not host dashboards and does not
communicate with Grafana.

Key Concept
Dashboard JSON
↓ Root dashboards.tf
↓ Reusable Module
↓ grafana_dashboard Resource
↓ Grafana Provider
↓ Grafana Cloud

Azure Storage Backend
↓ Stores Terraform State
↓ Separate from Grafana Deployment

Naming note
Names follow the requested design. The uploaded repo uses
per-team modules (./teams/<team>), alias pavilionpay and
grafana_dashboard.dashboards["<file>.json"].

Assumptions & unknowns
Dashboard-to-folder assignment (SRE, Tap2Play, VIP Connect) is illustrative: which dashboard lands in which folder is decided by the folder_uid the root layer passes in.
Terraform CLI uses both paths in one run: it reads dashboard config and talks to Grafana through the provider, and separately reads/writes state through the backend. The two paths never touch each other.
Grafana validates and stores dashboards; Azure Storage never receives dashboard JSON from Grafana and never calls Grafana. Provider credentials must stay out of source control.

Swimlane: who does what during a dashboard deployment
Left to right = time. Each lane is a responsibility boundary.

Assumptions & unknowns
Steps reflect the requested design. The backend lane only reads and writes state (init, plan/apply locking, final write); it never receives dashboards and never calls Grafana.
The provider lane is the only component that talks to the Grafana Cloud API. Who triggers the run (engineer vs CI pipeline) is not specified here.
Plan vs apply: both read state and refresh from Grafana; only apply sends create/update requests and writes new state.

From JSON file to live dashboard
Six steps, one analogy: building a house from a blueprint

1 · Dashboard JSON files
THE BLUEPRINT
Describes panels, queries and layout.
Lives in Git beside the Terraform code.

2 · Root dashboards.tf
THE ORDER FORM
Reads each file with file(...), groups by
team, picks folder_uid and provider alias.

3 · shared/dashboard-set
THE STANDARD BUILD KIT
Takes dashboards + folder_uid and makes
one dashboard per entry (for_each).

4 · grafana_dashboard
THE WORK ORDERS
One resource per dashboard. Terraform
tracks each one and plans create / update.

5 · Grafana provider
THE COURIER / TRANSLATOR
Logs in with a token and turns resources
into Grafana HTTP API requests.

6 · Grafana Cloud
THE FINISHED HOUSE
Validates the JSON, stores the dashboard
in its folder and shows it to users.
STATE STORAGE ONLY - a separate path (the filing cabinet that remembers what was built)
Azure Storage stores Terraform state only. It does not host dashboards and does not communicate with Grafana.

Assumptions & unknowns
Analogy: the JSON is the blueprint, Terraform the contractor following the order form, the provider the courier to the city office (Grafana), and the state file the ledger of what is already built.
Folders (for example SRE, Tap2Play, VIP Connect) are chosen by the folder_uid passed from the root layer. Names follow the requested design; see page 1 for repo differences.

Executive summary: Dashboards as Code
One slide for engineering leadership

Grafana dashboards are code: reviewed in Git, deployed by Terraform, stored in Grafana Cloud.
A shared module gives every team the same deployment pattern; state lives separately in Azure Storage.

Dashboard JSON files
what the dashboard looks like

Root dashboards.tf
reads files, assigns folder + provider

Why it matters
• Changes are reviewed in pull requests before they reach Grafana
• Same module for every team: consistent and repeatable
• terraform plan shows differences before anything changes
• Dashboards can be rebuilt from Git if Grafana is lost

State is separate
Azure Storage backend keeps Terraform state only.
It does not host dashboards and never talks to Grafana.
Losing or corrupting state is a Terraform problem, not a Grafana outage.

Guardrails to confirm
• Provider tokens kept out of source control (use secret store / variables)
• Remote state access limited to the pipeline and platform team
• Folder UIDs reviewed when a team or folder is added
• Who may apply (pipeline vs engineer) and approval steps documented

Assumptions & unknowns
Statements describe the requested architecture. Benefits listed are properties of the approach (Git review, plan, rebuild from code), not measured results from your environment.
Guardrails are recommendations to confirm; the uploaded repo currently contains literal provider tokens and contact-point API keys in .tf files that should be rotated and moved.
